narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist Luke, telling the story evenly and gravely.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: The Lord: calm authority, sorrowful in the Passion, serene after rising.

disciples.name: The disciples
disciples.note: The apostles speaking together: questioning, eager, bewildered.

angel.name: Angels at the tomb
angel.note: The two men in shining apparel, announcing the resurrection.

cleophas.name: Cleophas
cleophas.note: One of the two on the road to Emmaus, sad and surprised.

emmaus-disciples.name: The two disciples of Emmaus
emmaus-disciples.note: Cleophas and his companion: downcast on the road, then burning with joy.

1.t: And on the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came to the sepulchre, bringing the spices which they had prepared.

2.t: And they found the stone rolled back from the sepulchre.

3.t: And going in, they found not the body of the Lord Jesus.

4.t: And it came to pass, as they were astonished in their mind at this, behold, two men stood by them, in shining apparel.

5.t: And as they were afraid and bowed down their countenance towards the ground, they said unto them:
Why seek you the living with the dead?

6.t: He is not here, but is risen. Remember how he spoke unto you, when he was yet in Galilee,

7.t: Saying: The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men and be crucified and the third day rise again.

9.t: And going back from the sepulchre, they told all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.

10.t: And it was Mary Magdalen and Joanna and Mary of James and the other women that were with them, who told these things to the apostles.

11.t: And these words seemed to them as idle tales: and they did not believe them.

12.t: But Peter rising up, ran to the sepulchre and, stooping down, he saw the linen cloths laid by themselves: and went away wondering in himself at that which was come to pass.

13.t: And behold, two of them went, the same day, to a town which was sixty furlongs from Jerusalem, named Emmaus.

14.t: And they talked together of all these things which had happened.

15.t: And it came to pass that while they talked and reasoned with themselves, Jesus himself also, drawing near, went with them.

16.t: But their eyes were held, that they should not know him.

17.t: What are these discourses that you hold one with another as you walk and are sad?

18.t: And the one of them, whose name was Cleophas, answering, said to him:
Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things that have been done there in these days?

19.t: Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, who was a prophet, mighty in work and word before God and all the people.

20.t: And how our chief priests and princes delivered him to be condemned to death and crucified him.

21.t: But we hoped that it was he that should have redeemed Israel. And now besides all this, to-day is the third day since these things were done.

22.t: Yea and certain women also of our company affrighted us who, before it was light, were at the sepulchre,

23.t: And not finding his body, came, saying that they had all seen a vision of angels, who say that he is alive.

24.t: And some of our people went to the sepulchre and found it so as the women had said: but him they found not.

25.t: O foolish and slow of heart to believe in all things, Which the prophets have spoken.

26.t: Ought not Christ to have suffered these things and so, to enter into his glory?

27.t: And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded to them in all the scriptures the things that were concerning him.

28.t: And they drew nigh to the town whither they were going: and he made as though he would go farther.

29.t: Stay with us, because it is towards evening and the day is now far spent.
And he went in with them.

30.t: And it came to pass, whilst he was at table with them, he took bread and blessed and brake and gave to them.

31.t: And their eyes were opened: and they knew him. And he vanished out of their sight.

32.t: And they said one to the other:
Was not our heart burning within us, whilst he spoke in the way and opened to us the scriptures?

33.t: And rising up, the same hour, they went back to Jerusalem: and they found the eleven gathered together, and those that were with them,

34.t: The Lord is risen indeed and hath appeared to Simon.
34.q: the eleven greet the two with this news (so the Greek); the English could be read as the two speaking

35.t: And they told what things were done in the way: and how they knew him in the breaking of bread.

36.t: Now, whilst they were speaking these things, Jesus stood in the midst of them and saith to them:
Peace be to you. It is I: Fear not.

37.t: But they being troubled and frightened, supposed that they saw a spirit.

38.t: Why are you troubled, and why do thoughts arise in your hearts?

39.t: See my hands and feet, that it is I myself. Handle, and see: for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as you see me to have.

40.t: And when he had said this, he shewed them his hands and feet.

41.t: But while they yet believed not and wondered for joy, he said:
Have you here any thing to eat?

42.t: And they offered him a piece of a broiled fish and a honeycomb.

43.t: And when he had eaten before them, taking the remains, he gave to them.

44.t: These are the words which I spoke to you while I was yet with you, that all things must needs be fulfilled which are written in the law of Moses and in the prophets and in the psalms, concerning me.

45.t: Then he opened their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures.

46.t: Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer and to rise again from the dead, the third day:

47.t: And that penance and remission of sins should be preached in his name, unto all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.

48.t: And you are witnesses of these things.

49.t: And I send the promise of my Father upon you: but stay you in the city till you be endued with power from on high.

50.t: And he led them out as far as Bethania: and lifting up his hands, he blessed them.

51.t: And it came to pass, whilst he blessed them, he departed from them and was carried up to heaven.

52.t: And they adoring went back into Jerusalem with great joy.

53.t: And they were always in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.
